summary: AP2 assumes every LLM and agent can be turned against the user, so it puts the user's approval on a non-agentic Trusted Surface and binds every mandate to one checkout with hashes. Within that design, tampering with the checkout or payment and reusing a stolen mandate are well covered. The open problems sit before and after the signature: prompt injection that steers what the agent picks, replay at runtime because verifiers have no consume-once rule, no revocation of open mandates, no step-up in v0.2, and no retention rule for dispute evidence. No CVE or advisory exists for the repository; the published findings come from 2026 research papers and unreviewed GitHub issues.

threats.title: Manipulated discovery steers the agent
threats.description: Text in product listings or tool results (prompt injection) pushes the agent toward a brand, a pricier item or another user's credentials while it builds the cart.
preconditions: The agent reads untrusted merchant or tool content
Constraints are wide enough to allow the steered choice
threats.impact: A validly signed purchase that the user did not really want.
threats.implementerNotes: Signatures cover the final checkout, not the decision. Keep constraints narrow, show human-present approval for high value, and isolate the signer from the model.

threats.title: Manipulated checkout
threats.description: The agent or a man in the middle alters items or price between the merchant's signed checkout and the user approval.
threats.impact: User approves a different checkout than the merchant created.
threats.implementerNotes: The merchant signs checkout_jwt and checks checkout_hash against its latest checkout before completing.

threats.title: Manipulated payment
threats.description: The agent or Credential Provider changes payee, amount or instrument in transit.
preconditions: A party between the Trusted Surface and the processor is malicious
threats.impact: Funds go elsewhere or amount changes.
threats.implementerNotes: Processors and Credential Providers verify the user signature, the transaction_id binding and every constraint.

threats.title: Stolen Payment Mandate reused with another checkout
threats.description: An attacker replays a captured closed Payment Mandate against a different checkout.
preconditions: Mandate captured in transit or from logs
threats.implementerNotes: transaction_id names one checkout_jwt hash; open mandates must carry payment.reference.

threats.title: Replay of an accepted mandate at runtime
threats.description: Retries, concurrency or orchestration let the same accepted closed mandate be processed more than once.
threats.implementerNotes: The spec forbids overlapping presentations by the agent but defines no consume-once rule for verifiers; record each accepted mandate hash. Issue 346 reports the samples never consume accepted mandates.

threats.title: Double spend from one open mandate
threats.description: A compromised agent signs several closed mandates from one open mandate before any receipt arrives.
preconditions: Agent signer reachable by the model or attacker
threats.impact: Purchases beyond what the user approved.
threats.implementerNotes: The deterministic part of the agent must not sign overlapping mandates without a rejection receipt; Credential Providers, networks or processors may reject overlaps or invalidate tokens.

threats.title: Leakage of user intent through constraints
threats.description: A merchant learns the user's full budget or other merchants from open mandate constraints.
threats.implementerNotes: Selective disclosure is mandatory for constraints; decoy digests may be added; disclose only what the verifier needs.

threats.title: Rainbow-table guessing of digests
threats.description: An observer guesses checkout contents from checkout_hash or disclosure digests.
threats.implementerNotes: Salted digests per RFC 9901; the two spec documents disagree on deterministic signatures (issue 268). Use ECDSA and add entropy.

threats.title: No revocation of an open mandate
threats.description: A user changes their mind or the agent is compromised, but an open mandate stays valid until exp.
threats.impact: Purchases after the user withdrew consent.
threats.implementerNotes: Use the shortest exp the task allows; Credential Providers and networks can refuse tokens. ERC-8226 shows an on-chain revoke for comparison.

threats.title: Agent key theft
threats.description: An attacker obtains the agent private key named in cnf.
preconditions: Key stored where the model or host can reach it
threats.impact: Attacker can close any open mandate within its constraints.
threats.implementerNotes: Proof of possession binds the mandate to the key, not to the agent's integrity. Keep the key in deterministic code or hardware; keep open mandates short and narrow.

threats.title: Fallback abuse through unresolved_constraint
threats.description: An attacker forces repeated unresolved_constraint errors so the user is asked again and again, or into a non-agentic flow with weaker checks.
threats.impact: Approval fatigue; users approve without reading.
threats.implementerNotes: v0.2 defines no step-up and no limit on fallbacks; Trusted Surfaces should show the full checkout each time.

threats.title: Dispute evidence not retained
threats.description: Mandates and receipts are not stored, so nobody can prove what the user approved.
threats.impact: Disputes fall back to network rules without evidence.
threats.implementerNotes: Retention and retrieval are out of scope; agree retention with your network and processor.

scenarios.title: Listing text upgrades the purchase
preconditions: Open mandate allows any item from one merchant up to 300 USD
steps: A listing includes text telling assistants to prefer the premium model
The agent builds a checkout for the premium model at 295 USD
The agent signs a closed mandate inside the constraints
Merchant and Credential Provider verify successfully
scenarios.impact: A valid, fully evidenced purchase the user would not have chosen; mandates prove approval of limits, not of the choice.

scenarios.title: Retry storm charges twice
preconditions: Verifier keeps no record of accepted mandates
steps: The agent receives no receipt and retries
The same closed mandate is accepted again

scenarios.title: Compromised agent within a long open mandate
preconditions: Open mandate with a week-long exp and a budget constraint
Agent key reachable on the host
steps: Attacker closes mandates with allowed merchants up to the budget
The user cannot revoke the open mandate
scenarios.impact: Loss up to the budget before exp.

research.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
research.finding: 48 threats in five families across five architectures, eight in the High band; valid signatures do not guarantee intent when the pre-authorization context is manipulated.

research.title: Zero-Trust Runtime Verification for Agentic Payment Protocols
research.finding: Replay and context-redirect gaps from retries and concurrency; consume-once nonces at about 3.8 ms in simulation.

research.title: Whispers of Wealth: Red-Teaming Google's Agent Payments Protocol via Prompt Injection
research.finding: Branded Whisper and Vault Whisper attacks steer product ranking and extract user data from an AP2 shopping agent.

research.title: Signing the Transaction but Not the Decision: Whisper Attacks and a Binding Defense for AP2
research.finding: Product-description text steers sample agents into credential fetches, cart divergence and upgrades; proposes A-VIP session binding.

research.title: A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols
research.finding: Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2; 40 new formal-consistency findings across 86 cases.

research.title: SoK: Security of Autonomous LLM Agents in Agentic Commerce
research.finding: 12 cross-layer attack vectors across agent payment protocols including AP2.
